facts.material: natural stone (Saturnia; charcoal gray to black, mottled with brown and white flecks); petrographic identity from lab analysis not stated
facts.function: building stone to be cut into countertops and surfaces
facts.form: slab approx. 115-122 x 65-75 in, 0.75 or 1.5 in thick, top face polished, sides simply cut or sawn, not cut to size
facts.end_use: kitchen countertops, bathroom surfaces, office furniture surfaces

gri_path: GRI 1: polished (surface-worked) stone slab is worked monumental or building stone of heading 6802, not heading 2515/2516 (chapter 25 covers stone merely cut/sawn) and not 6801 setts/curbs

GRI 6: under 6802.9 (other) the subheading turns on the stone type: marble/travertine (6802.91), calcareous (6802.92), granite (6802.93), other stone (6802.99); assumed lab identified a non-granite stone (e.g., gabbro), giving 6802.99.00

rejected_alternatives.reason: applies only if CBP lab identifies the stone as granite (as with Branco Fortaleza in N358799); lab result not given in description
not marble, travertine or alabaster on the description
top face is polished, so it is worked beyond simple sawing; chapter 25 excluded

missing_facts: What did the CBP laboratory determine the Saturnia stone is composed of (granite vs. other stone such as gabbro, gneiss, quartzite)?
classification.rationale: A slab with a polished top face and sawn edges is worked building stone of heading 6802, classified under 6802.9x by stone type since it is not in the 6802.2x cut-to-size group. N353775 (same template, White Spring stone, identical dimensions) and N358799 show CBP relies on laboratory identification to choose between granite (6802.93.00.10) and other stone (6802.99.00.90). The lab result for Saturnia is not stated; dark black stones sold as granite are frequently gabbro, so 6802.99.00.90 is the best guess, but 6802.93.00.10 applies if the lab found granite.
